props.sub: BearMinion turns your Astro site into its own editor. Change text, sections and images on the page while it runs on your machine. Every edit is saved as **JSON in your repository**, and the build is a plain static site.

props.intro: The editor is built from your theme's own schemas, so it can only write content that your site renders and that passes validation.

Run npm run dev, press Ctrl+E (Cmd+E on a Mac) and edit the page in place. Ctrl+S saves to content/.
Commit and push. Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages or any static host builds it with npm run build.

props.body: The editor and its API exist only while the dev server runs. The build is static HTML, CSS and images.
props.heading: What ships to your visitors.

items.label: of editor code in the build

props.heading: Questions, answered.

items.a: In your repository. Each page is a JSON file in content/pages/, the site settings are in content/site.json, and uploaded images go to src/assets/uploads/. You review and commit them like any other change.
No. The editor and its API run only in astro dev. The production build has no editor, no server and no database in it.
items.q: Does the editor end up on my live site?

items.a: Anyone with the repository and the dev server running. The editor only answers requests from your own machine, so other sites and other computers on your network cannot change your content. Editing a live site without a local copy is planned.
items.q: Who can edit, and from where?

items.a: Yes. The template is yours once the site is created: change its components and styles, or add a section type with a schema, defaults and a component, and the editor picks it up. See [Building a theme](https://docs.bearminion.com/themes/).
items.q: Can I use my own design?

items.a: Anywhere that serves a static site: Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages or your own server. The host runs npm run build and publishes the dist folder.
Nothing. BearMinion is open source under the [MIT license](https://github.com/langehelp-software/bearminion/blob/main/LICENSE), and the site it creates is yours.

props.more: Anything else is in the docs.
